steps: 1. VISUAL PRE-ATTENTION: 'I've seen something similar to that before' - same paper, color, typeset triggers the hypothesis that two pages belong together.
2. ZOOM & CHECK TELLS: 'I zoom in and I check a few things' - seals, stamps, margins, handwriting identity.
3. READ THE BEGINNING OF THE PAGE: does it start mid-sentence/mid-clause (continuation) or fresh?
4. READ THE ENDING OF THE PAGE: does it end with a colon, an incomplete construction ('with the following and a column'), or a full stop?

5. SEMANTIC LINKING: page 1 ends with '...the following:' and page 2 opens with a numbered list (1. Mr. XYZ, 2. Miss Jane Doe) -> the list completes the sentence -> same document. Semantic completion outranks everything.

6. FOLIO ARITHMETIC AS CONFIRMATION ONLY: 'I see the page numbers sequential. This is 1 over 6, so this has to be 2 over 6, it cannot be 3 over 6, unless page 2 ends with a colon and page 3 continues' - sequence is a cross-check, never the discovery signal.
human_continuity_protocol.rule: The engine must mimic THIS order: visual hypothesis -> tells -> begin/end reading -> semantic linking -> folio confirmation. A regex folio scan is step 6, not step 1.
human_continuity_protocol.v2_header_first: Stage 3 refined: the HEADER (same or ~99% close) is the primary family key; body begin/end links pages WITHIN that family; topic continuity second. Tolerances: skew, low quality, different camera/page color acceptable when header + topic match.
